::: {#sol-choices}

[SGD](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-sgd) changes only the weights and biases of the two `nn.Linear` layers.
These numbers are set before training starts, and stay as set:

-   the [width](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-width) of the [hidden layer](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-hidden-layer), `width`;
-   the [learning rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate), `lr`;
-   the number of [epochs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch), `n_epochs`;
-   the [minibatch](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-minibatch) size, `batch_size`;
-   the random seed, `seed`;
-   the sizes of the training and [validation sets](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-validation-set), `r py$n_train` and `r py$n_val`.

The first four are [hyperparameters](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/model-selection.html#sec-hyperparameters):
settings that we choose,
rather than learn from the data.
So are choices that are not numbers,
such as SGD itself,
the [ReLU](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-relu) activation and the single hidden layer.
The seed is not a setting of that kind.
No seed suits new data better than another,
so a seed chosen for its validation score has been fitted to noise.
The set sizes are a choice about the data, not the model.

:::
